note.question: What determines equilibrium distortion of algorithmic price advice when a human manager bears attention and adjustment costs?
note.overview: An informed algorithmic advisor strategically chooses a recommendation to induce attention and repricing by a manager who has private local information and costly adjustment. The paper defines and structurally estimates a perfect Bayesian equilibrium in linear reporting strategies.

components.label: Perfect Bayesian equilibrium in linear algorithmic reporting and sequential managerial attention
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Perfect Bayesian equilibrium in linear algorithmic reporting and sequential managerial attention. An equilibrium is a triple (λ,c(r),Y_0(c,r)): λ maximizes the advisor's expected profit given the manager's rules, and the update cutoff and copy region are optimal under beliefs x=λr. Lemmas and Propositions 1-2 characterize attention, copying, and negative selection; estimation imposes no profitable local deviation in λ.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: The algorithm privately observes x and sends a linear recommendation r=x/λ. The manager observes the current price, r, and cost shock c; decides whether to pay attention and learn y; then either copies r or pays an additional cost to learn z and manually chooses the posterior-optimal price. The algorithm anticipates these responses when selecting λ. Although primitive profit objectives are aligned, asymmetric adjustment costs create an endogenous conflict.
